content.text:
Found it — your settings force checkpoints onto GitHub, and the resolver can't produce `entire://` URLs at all.

**Bottom line:** Your normal pushes already go through the mirror (origin is `entire://aws-ap-southeast-2.entire.io/gh/entireio/cli`). The SSH-to-GitHub traffic is the checkpoint machinery, caused by `checkpoint_remote: {"provider": "github", ...}` in `.entire/settings.json:5-8` — and there is currently no way to configure a checkpoint remote that routes via `entire://`. It's a feature gap, not a settings mistake.

The exact chain:

- At pre-push, `resolvePushSettings` calls `remote.PushURL(ctx, "origin")` (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/checkpoint_remote.go:70`).
- `PushURL` tries to derive the checkpoint URL from origin's protocol, but `entire://` is not a "derivable" transport — only SSH and HTTPS are (`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/util.go:284-286`, `util.go:288-302`).
- So it falls into `resolveProviderCheckpointURL` (`util.go:226`), which maps provider `github` → host `github.com` (`util.go:421-430`) and picks a transport by precedence (`util.go:340-361`): token → reuse an existing remote's scheme for that host → default SSH.
- Your git config has URL-named promisor remotes left by `filtered_fetches` (`remote.git@github.com:entireio/cli-checkpoints.git.promisor true` etc.), so step 2 matches SSH — and even without them, step 3 defaults to SSH anyway. Result: checkpoints push/fetch over `git@github.com:entireio/cli-checkpoints.git`.
- `GetCheckpointRemote` (`cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go:1399`) only accepts `{provider, repo}` with provider ∈ {github, gitlab} — no raw-URL form, no "entire" provider. So no settings.json edit can route the checkpoint repo through the mirror today.

Your options:

1. **Delete the `checkpoint_remote` block** — checkpoints then push to origin, i.e. through the `entire://` mirror, but they land on `entire/checkpoints/v1` of `entireio/cli` itself instead of the separate `cli-checkpoints` repo. Tradeoff: you lose the separate-repo isolation, gain full mirror routing immediately.
2. **Keep the separate repo, add the feature** — teach `checkpoint_remote` to accept an `entire://` target (e.g. `{"url": "entire://<cluster>/gh/entireio/cli-checkpoints"}`), plus create a push-through mirror for `cli-checkpoints`. That's a CLI change in `checkpoint/remote/util.go` + `settings.go`.

Side observations: the `remote.entire://eukanuba.partial.to/...` promisor entry is a stale leftover from an old mirror host, and `remote.origin.entiredb-original-url` confirms origin was already migrated off SSH — so the checkpoint path is the only SSH user left in this repo's config.

Want me to implement option 2 (an `entire://`-capable checkpoint remote), or just flip you to option 1?

18		ProtocolHTTPS = "https"
19		// ProtocolEntire is the scheme of Entire's git remote helper (entire://).
20		// These URLs carry a forge/namespace prefix before owner/repo.
21		ProtocolEntire = "entire"
22	)

24	// Info holds the parsed components of a git remote URL.
25	// Host is the hostname only (never includes a port). Port is empty unless the
26	// source URL specified an explicit non-default port. Callers that need the
27	// combined "host[:port]" form should use HostPort.
28	//
29	// Forge is the short identifier of the upstream forge ("gh", "et", ...) used
30	// by the Entire trails API. It is populated from the path prefix on entire://
31	// URLs (entire://host/<forge>/owner/repo) and from a hostname lookup on
32	// direct git URLs (github.com → "gh"). It is empty for direct git URLs to
33	// unrecognized hosts, and for entire:// URLs without a forge segment.
34	type Info struct {
35		Protocol string
36		Host     string
37		Port     string
38		Forge    string
39		Owner    string
40		Repo     string
41	}

43	// hostToForge maps direct git hostnames to their forge identifier on the
44	// trails API. entire:// URLs carry the forge in the path instead and bypass
45	// this map.
46	var hostToForge = map[string]string{
47		"github.com": "gh",
48	}
49	
50	// forgeToHost is the reverse of hostToForge: it maps a forge identifier back to
51	// its canonical public host. Used to recover the real forge host from an
52	// entire:// remote, whose Host is the Entire cluster rather than the forge.
53	var forgeToHost = func() map[string]string {
54		m := make(map[string]string, len(hostToForge))
55		for host, forge := range hostToForge {
56			m[forge] = host
57		}
58		return m

61	// IsSupportedForge reports whether forge is a known short forge id (e.g. "gh")
62	// understood by the trails API. It rejects forge hostnames ("github.com") and
63	// any other unrecognized value, so callers parsing a bare forge/owner/repo
64	// triple can fail clearly instead of forwarding a malformed forge to the API.
65	func IsSupportedForge(forge string) bool {
66		_, ok := forgeToHost[forge]

68	}

70	// CanonicalHost returns the canonical public host of the upstream forge.
71	//
72	// For direct git URLs this is just Host. For entire:// remotes — whose Host is
73	// the Entire cluster (e.g. aws-us-east-2.entire.io) rather than the forge — it

78		if host, ok := forgeToHost[i.Forge]; ok {

112		rawURL = strings.TrimSpace(rawURL)

136		if err != nil {
137			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid URL: %s", RedactURL(rawURL))
138		}
139		if u.Scheme == "" {
140			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no protocol in URL: %s", RedactURL(rawURL))
141		}
142

144		forge := hostToForge[u.Hostname()]
145		if u.Scheme == ProtocolEntire {
146			// entire:// URLs encode the forge as the first path segment.
147			forge, pathPart = splitForgePrefix(pathPart)
148		}
149		owner, repo, err := splitOwnerRepo(pathPart)
150		if err != nil {
151			return nil, err
152		}
153	
154		return &Info{Protocol: u.Scheme, Host: u.Hostname(), Port: u.Port(), Forge: forge, Owner: owner, Repo: repo}, nil
155	}
156	
157	// splitForgePrefix returns the leading forge/namespace segment of an entire://
158	// URL path and the remainder (e.g. "gh/owner/repo" -> "gh", "owner/repo").
159	// Paths without a separator are returned with an empty forge.
160	func splitForgePrefix(path string) (forge, rest string) {
161		if forge, rest, found := strings.Cut(path, "/"); found {
162			return forge, rest
163		}
164		return "", path
165	}

167	// RedactURL removes credentials and query parameters from a URL for safe logging.
168	// SCP-style SSH URLs (e.g., git@github.com:org/repo.git) are returned as-is
169	// since they contain no embedded credentials.
170	func RedactURL(rawURL string) string {
171		// SCP-style SSH: user@host:path — no credentials to redact.
172		if strings.Contains(rawURL, ":") && !strings.Contains(rawURL, "://") {
173			return rawURL
174		}
175	
176		u, err := url.Parse(rawURL)
177		if err != nil {
178			return "<unparseable>"
179		}
180		u.User = nil
181		u.RawQuery = ""
182		return u.Scheme + "://" + u.Host + u.Path
183	}

186	// given git remote. The forge is the short id used by the trails API ("gh",
187	// "et", ...); it is derived from the hostname for direct git URLs or from the
188	// path prefix on entire:// URLs. It is empty for unrecognized hosts.
189	// For example, git@github.com:org/my-repo.git returns ("gh", "org", "my-repo").
190	func ResolveRemoteRepo(ctx context.Context, remoteName string) (forge, owner, repo string, err error) {
191		rawURL, err := GetRemoteURL(ctx, remoteName)
192		if err != nil {
193			return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("get remote URL for %q: %w", remoteName, err)
194		}
195		info, err := ParseURL(rawURL)
196		if err != nil {
197			return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("parse remote URL: %w", err)
198		}
199		return info.Forge, info.Owner, info.Repo, nil
200	}

203		path = strings.TrimSuffix(path, ".git")
204		parts := strings.SplitN(path, "/", 2)
205		if len(parts) != 2 || parts[0] == "" || parts[1] == "" {
206			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("cannot parse owner/repo from path: %s", path)
207		}
208		// Reject control characters (newlines, ANSI escapes, ...). The SCP-style
209		// branch in ParseURL bypasses net/url.Parse's built-in control-char
210		// rejection, so a crafted origin URL could otherwise smuggle a newline or
211		// escape into owner/repo and, via plain-text consumers like `entire
212		// agent-help`, into an agent's context or a user's terminal. This shared
213		// chokepoint protects every caller; the tainted bytes are not echoed back.
214		if strings.IndexFunc(parts[0]+"/"+parts[1], unicode.IsControl) >= 0 {
215			return "", "", errors.New("invalid control character in remote owner/repo")
216		}
217		return parts[0], parts[1], nil
